text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's Prime Minister Ivan Kostov called on parliament to change Bulgaria's constitution to allow foreigners to buy land in the country.

-- Bulgaria's state arms supplier Armimex said it had not authorised two Lithuanians arrested in the United States on Friday to sell Bulgarian anti aircraft missiles to a Columbian drugs cartel. Kostov said the cabinet would launch an investigation into the Armimex contracts.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it had bought 15 million marks from Bulgarians in the first day of the introduction of a currency board system.
-- Bulgarian police said they seized six truckloads of counterfeit alchohol worth some 120 million levs in the southeastern village of Venets.
-- Germany may extend some 1.3 million marks to support small private businesses, a Bulgarian Economic Chamber official said.

-- Hundreds of Bulgarians gathered on Sunday night in the northeast port of Varna for traditional hippy celebrations of the July 1 morning. Police said one Bulgarian died from a drugs overdose on the Varna beach.

-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to approve a new state coat of arms at the beginning of August, National History Museum director Bozhidar Dimitrov said. President Petar Stoyanov discussed projects for the state crest on Tuesday with representatives of the main political parties.
-- Bulgaria has set up a rapid response squad of 100 police motorcyclists to crack down on car theft and armed robbery in Sofia, Sofia police chief Emil Tanev said.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov leaves for an official visit to Greece today, the first visit of a Bulgarian president to Greece since 1989.

-- Bulgaria's state carrier Balkan Airlines said it would launch an initiative to set up an alliance with carriers from neighbouring Balkan countries similar to the Scandinavian SAS Airlines in a move to compete with Western airline companies.
-- South Korea's Hyundai Corp signed an agreement to buy a 70 percent stake in Bulgaria's Elprom-Trapho power transformer maker for $2.9 million, the Privatisation Agency said.
